Liam to run controlled 1k rps load with current retry settings and report results
Schedule canary with VPC fallback enabled for next Thursday 9/25
Share security whitepaper and SOC2 cert copy with Joan

header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Daniel Ortiz (Nexera CTO), Priya Rao (Nexera SRE), Amir Khaled (Nexera Backend), Joan Li (Nexera Compliance)
summary: Weekly POC sync to follow up on yesterday's alert storm. Root causes discussed: duplicated telemetry leading to false alarms, aggressive client retry behavior causing queue buildup and timeouts, and an incomplete VPC fallback test. Agreed next steps: telemetry export, targeted load run with adjusted retry budgets, schedule VPC fallback canary, and share security docs for Private deployment evaluation.
topics: Retry budget tuning and backoff windows
KV cache warmup and cold-start throttling
VPC fallback plan and canary schedule
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we want to go over yesterday's alert storm and set the canary for the vpc fallback.
[00:21] Daniel: yeah, thanks Maya. we saw a big number of 5xx spikes across the staging tier, not just single instances, there was a pattern.
[00:34] Priya: to add, our monitoring showed a lot of duplicate traces — the telemetry ingestion looked like it re-submitted events 2x-3x which made the alerting blow up. might be in our forwarder but could also be some sampler configuration.
[00:49] Speaker 1: mhm.
[00:52] Liam: quick clarification, when you say duplicate, is that raw logs duplicated or the metrics series?
[00:57] Priya: mostly traces and error counts — like the same request id showed up multiple times, but tokenized counters also went up.
[01:08] Maya: okay that explains the noise. on the Redwood side we saw a correlated increase in retry traffic from the client SDK which, combined with a cold kv cache, produced queued requests and some timeouts.
[01:25] Amir: our client currently has naive retries — it retries on 502/503 with no jitter and only small backoff. once the first retry kicks in, we get a cascade.
[01:34] Liam: yeah that cascade is classic hotkey/retry spiral — the runtime's queue fills, then kernel scheduling delays, then tail latency spikes and 5xx returns.
[01:44] Maya: so two threads — the telemetry duplication making ops over-sensitive, and the retry spiral making real user traffic hit the SLO. both need addressing.
[01:53] Daniel: we attempted the VPC fallback yesterday but the switch over didn't complete — some routes stayed pinned to hosted endpoints and we lost visibility.
[02:05] Sofia: quick note, sometimes the route table needs an updated policy; we've seen sticky sessions in their load balancer configs.
[02:14] Joan: from compliance, we need the canary to be documented and auditable — exact times, who executed, and the rollback conditions. also need to see SOC2 and KMS integration info before we approve Private.
[02:31] Maya: absolutely, we'll provide that. I'll attach the SOC2 and the KMS/HSM integration guide.
[02:37] Priya: for the retry behavior, what do you recommend? lower retry count, exponential with jitter, or a client-side circuit breaker?
[02:47] Liam: combination — smaller retry budget per minute, exponential backoff with full jitter, and client-side sliding window to stop retries when server returns sustained 5xx. on the server side we can add early rejection and a retry budget token so retries don't overrun the queue.
[03:05] Amir: can Redwood provide a suggested client config or SDK patch we can try? shipping that internally is faster for us than reworking the infra.
[03:12] Maya: yes, Liam can share a sample config and the SDK snippet. we'll include a recommended backoff formula: base=100ms, max=2s, full jitter, and max attempts=2 for idempotent calls.
[03:27] Daniel: that seems reasonable. but we also have some long-running batch calls that can't be retried idempotently.
[03:35] Liam: mark those as no-retry on the client; use async job semantics or a dedicated high-latency route with higher concurrency.
[03:44] Priya: about the KV cache warmup — we suspect many requests were cold-starting with large context windows so the runtime did extra work and throttled others. any way to pre-warm?
[03:56] Liam: we can pre-warm observed hot keys with a small synthetic traffic pattern or use prefix caching for common prompts. also setting a gentle ramp for new workers helps.
[04:07] Maya: action: we'll provide a script to warm the kv cache in staging prior to the canary.
[04:13] Amir: good. also, during the spike we noticed spike TTL on the load balancer which increased connection churn.
[04:21] Maya: okay we'll include connection pooling recommendations.
[04:24] [04:24] (crosstalk)
[04:26] Priya: one more telemetry detail — the trace IDs were sometimes truncated by our forwarder; could that cause duplicates?
[04:34] Liam: possibly, if the forwarder retries without preserving the original trace id or if the id hashing collides. we can correlate by client timestamp and payload hash to dedupe in the short term.
[04:45] Maya: good interim step — we'll give a dedupe script and Priya can run it to verify how much noise is synthetic.
[04:53] Daniel: regarding the VPC fallback, what exactly failed yesterday? we got a partial switch and then some requests timed out.
[04:59] Sofia: on our end, routing policies rolled out but the fallback target had a slightly different model alias; routing didn't match and requests hit a default which returned 502.
[05:11] Maya: that alias mismatch is the culprit — we should validate model alias mapping as part of the canary checklist.
[05:18] Amir: is there a dry-run mode to perform alias validation without switching traffic?
[05:23] Liam: yes, we have a dry-run that simulates routing and reports mismatches. we'll run that first.
[05:29] Maya: next up, the planned load run — Liam, you suggested a 1k rps replay with varied retry settings to observe queueing. timeline?
[05:38] Liam: I can run it tomorrow in a controlled window; will produce latency percentiles and queue length heatmaps. need access to staging endpoints and a seed dataset.
[05:47] Daniel: we'll provide the dataset and open access to the staging VPC for the replay window.
[05:52] Priya: make sure the replay includes some hotkey skew (5% of keys get 40% of the traffic) to reproduce the hotkey behavior.
[06:02] Liam: noted — we'll add a zipf distribution.
[06:05] Joan: compliance question — if we run the canary in Private mode, does Redwood ship any PII in logs? we need to know what fields are redacted.
[06:15] Maya: by default we redact identified PII from logs; for Private deployment you control retention and can point to a KMS. we'll share the logging redaction docs.
[06:25] Joan: ok please include the specific log fields that are redacted and the retention window.
[06:30] Maya: will do.
[06:33] [06:33] (brief pause)
[06:36] Priya: for alerting, we want to lower noise thresholds but not miss real incidents. if duplicates are the cause we should dedupe before thresholds.
[06:45] Liam: agree — dedupe at ingestion and then use alert windows (e.g., sustained error rate > 0.5% for 3 minutes) rather than single-second bursts.
[06:56] Amir: liability note — some background jobs will still requeue on failure; we should ensure we have idempotency tokens to avoid duplicates at the application level.
[07:06] Maya: good reminder.
[07:08] Daniel: any blockers to scheduling the canary for next Thursday?
[07:13] Priya: staging access and the telemetry export are the only blockers for us.
[07:19] Maya: we will send the telemetry now, and Liam will run the load test. once results look good, we run dry-run routing validation, then canary with documented rollback.
[07:30] Sofia: I'll prepare the canary runbook and add rollback conditions: error rate > 1% sustained for 2 minutes, or tail P95 > 2x baseline.
[07:40] Joan: and include audit entries for who executed the run.
[07:44] Maya: yes.
[07:46] [07:46] (short interruption, background noise)
[07:50] Liam: I'll also try a small change on the runtime — enable early-reject for retry traffic families to preserve queue headroom, but that will be behind a feature flag.
[08:02] Amir: will that change affect throughput for legitimate long-tail requests?
[08:07] Liam: it might slightly increase tail errors for non-idempotent long requests; that's why we do the canary on low percent traffic first.
[08:14] Daniel: what's the rollback time if we see regression? can we flip back in under 5 minutes?
[08:19] Maya: yes, the routing rollback is automated and we can flip in under 2 minutes if conditions met.
[08:25] Priya: regarding the dedupe script, can you provide expected output format and a quick sanity dashboard so we can see before/after?
[08:34] Maya: we'll provide a CSV and a short grafana panel config.
[08:39] [08:39] (crosstalk)
[08:42] Liam: lastly, for SDK changes, we can push a pre-release tag with recommended retry config; if Nexera wants, we can host a tiny container with the patched client for an easy rollout.
[08:55] Amir: that would be helpful. less friction for devs.
[08:59] Maya: summary — immediate deliverables: telemetry export, dedupe script, SDK config + pre-release, kv warmup script, 1k rps load report, canary runbook and dry-run validation.
[09:15] Daniel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:18] Maya: ok we'll send the artifacts and schedule the run. any other questions?
[09:22] Joan: just the security docs please.
[09:25] Maya: noted. thanks all. meeting adjourned.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
